episodes.summary: We've spent the last few days telling you to watch one thing: the July 29th Fed decision, as the live test of whether Bitcoin still trades like an inflation hedge or like a leveraged bet on risk appetite. It has now resolved, and it resolved about as hawkish as a "hold" can get.

episodes.title: Strategic Power, Energy, and Institutional Change — July 30, 2026
episodes.summary: The thread running through today is that the AI buildout's costs are compounding from three directions at once. The grid is metering it physically, the chips are getting more expensive rather than cheaper, and the inflation those two things help generate is keeping the Federal Reserve hawkish.

episodes.title: Semiconductors & Compute Infrastructure — July 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the lithography chokepoint, because a report out this week says it just got a crack in it. China has begun mass-producing its first domestic immersion DUV lithography tools, the workhorse machines that pattern everything from legacy logic to DRAM.

episodes.title: Enterprise Technology & Software — July 30, 2026
episodes.summary: All week this show has been asking the same question: is the industry's AI capital spending actually converting into revenue, or is it outrunning the demand behind it? Last night we got the first hard answer, and it didn't settle the question cleanly — it split the hyperscalers in two.

episodes.title: Robotics & Physical AI — July 30, 2026
episodes.summary: The theme this week is a widening gap between how fast capital is repricing autonomy and how slowly the operating economics are catching up. Nowhere is that clearer than in defense tech, where the boldest mark of the year just landed, so let's start there.

episodes.title: Private Credit & the Corporate Credit Cycle — July 30, 2026
episodes.summary: We've been telling you for two days running to watch one number: whether Ares Capital's non-accrual rate, sitting at 2.1% of cost after the first quarter, would move up or down when the second-quarter print landed. It landed yesterday, and it moved up.

episodes.title: Private Equity & the Deal Economy — July 30, 2026
episodes.summary: KKR reported this morning, and it's the print this show has been building toward all week. The headline question is whether cash realization is genuinely accelerating, or whether the reported numbers are being flattered by an accounting change.

episodes.title: The Throughline (daily synthesis) — July 30, 2026
episodes.summary: Start with the macro backdrop. Strategic Power leads with the physical constraint underneath all of it: the Energy Department forced PJM's data centers onto backup generators during a record-threatening heatwave in June, and PJM's board just proposed a formal curtailment framework for new large loads.
